verdicts.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside a package inherit the package's version.
verdicts.evidence: The linked concepts page says components are shipped inside the package's plugin: "The provider plugin contains custom resources, functions, and components." Packages are also installed and upgraded as whole units (for example, `pulumi package add ...@v2.0.0` or a single SDK version). It follows that components share the package's single version, but the page never states the "unit of versioning and distribution" wording outright.
verdicts.framing_note: The source describes packages as a plugin plus SDK, with components inside the plugin and versioned per package. The claim's 'unit of versioning and distribution' wording is a reasonable summary, but the page doesn't say it word for word.

verdicts.text: Cross-references: link targets exist for /docs/iac/concepts/packages/, /docs/iac/concepts/components/, /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/, /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/, and /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
verdicts.evidence: I found a content file for all five targets: content/docs/iac/concepts/packages/_index.md ("Pulumi packages"), content/docs/iac/concepts/components/_index.md ("Components"), content/docs/idp/concepts/private-registry.md ("Private Registry"), content/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish.md (auto-generated, "Publish a package to the Private Registry"), and content/docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages.md ("Publishing to the Pulumi Registry").
verdicts.framing_note: Only checked that the link target pages exist. The source_hint page (packaging-components) links to /docs/iac/concepts/packages/ and /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/, which agrees with these targets.

verdicts.text: Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), and each is versioned and released differently.
verdicts.evidence: The sibling page packaging-components.md covers "Source-based plugin packages" (shipped as source code, pulled with `pulumi package add` from a Git URL and revision) and "Executable-based plugin packages" (a pre-built plugin binary plus SDKs published per language), so the two packages ship and release in different ways. This backs the claim, but the backing comes only from Pulumi's own docs pages; I didn't check it against product source.
verdicts.intuition_flag: "Two flavors" leaves out native language packages. The sibling page lists those as a third distribution option, but they aren't Pulumi packages in the plugin/schema sense, so the claim still holds.

verdicts.text: Pulumi packages come in two flavors: source-based and executable-based plugin packages.
verdicts.evidence: The sibling Packaging Components guide gives the same split. It lists a source-based plugin package ("a Pulumi package distributed as source") and an executable-based plugin package ("a Pulumi package whose plugin is a pre-built executable"). Its third option, native language packages, is explicitly "Not a Pulumi package", so two kinds of Pulumi package is consistent with it.
verdicts.framing_note: Only other Pulumi docs back this up; it was not checked against product source. The claim's own two links point to anchors that exist in the sibling page.

verdicts.text: The first step of publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry is applying a semver Git tag (e.g., `v1.2.3`) to the repository.
verdicts.evidence: The Private Registry concept page agrees: "Pulumi uses git tags for versioning components... The tag must adhere to the semantic versioning standard plus a 'v' prefix (e.g. `v1.2.3`)". Its quick start also tags first (`git tag v1.0.0`) and then runs `pulumi package publish`, and its troubleshooting section lists `error: no version tag found`. This is corroboration from another Pulumi docs page, not product source: I couldn't check the CLI source because GitHub code search was rate-limited (HTTP 429).

verdicts.text: `pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference, transcribed from pulumi/pulumi source, says: "This command publishes a package to the Private Registry. The package can be a provider or a schema." It also shows that the command extracts or reads the package schema and takes readme and installation-configuration files, which is the metadata the claim says gets sent to Pulumi Cloud.
verdicts.framing_note: Source: "Publish a package to the Private Registry". The claim restates this as sending package metadata to Pulumi Cloud, which hosts the Private Registry.

verdicts.text: Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated `pulumi package add` reference (built from pulumi/pulumi CLI help) says a Git version "can either be a tag (in semver format), or a Git commit hash." So branches and non-semver tags are not listed as supported, which contradicts "any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version."
verdicts.intuition_flag: The CLI help text may lag behind the code. Someone should check how pulumi/pulumi resolves Git refs (branch and non-semver tag handling) before accepting or rejecting this line.

verdicts.text: Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.
verdicts.evidence: The local docs only mention tags ("`pulumi package add <repo_url>[/path/to/component]@<release-version>`", "a git tag (or even a local path) is enough"). Nothing I found in the repo or in pulumi/pulumi issues/PRs confirms that branch names or arbitrary non-semver refs work in `Pulumi.yaml` `packages` entries. Code search was rate-limited (HTTP 429), so I couldn't read the git-source version-resolution code.
verdicts.source: repo:content/docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/source-based-plugin.md L513-525; gh issue/pr list -R pulumi/pulumi (package add git branch/commit)
verdicts.intuition_flag: As far as I recall, Pulumi's git plugin source turns commit hashes into pseudo-versions (v0.0.0-x<hash>). I'm not sure branch names are supported, so "any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit)" may claim too much. Worth checking pkg/workspace plugin git-source code.

verdicts.text: Executable-based package releases are produced by a CI/CD pipeline that builds the plugin, generates the SDKs, and pushes everything to the relevant feeds.
verdicts.evidence: The release workflow in Pulumi's provider boilerplate (the reference template for executable-based packages) runs on a `v*.*.*` tag push. Its jobs run `make provider` (Build Provider), then `make generate_${{ matrix.language }}` (Generate SDK) for nodejs, python, dotnet, go and java, and then publish the results. That matches the build → generate SDKs → push-to-feeds pipeline the claim describes.
verdicts.framing_note: This describes a typical practice, not a hard product requirement. Pulumi's reference template follows it, but custom pipelines can differ.

verdicts.text: Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says `pulumi package publish` "publishes a package to the Private Registry. The package can be a provider or a schema," and "When <provider> is specified as a local path, Pulumi executes the provider binary to extract its package schema." So the command accepts binary (executable-based) providers, and the Private Registry is part of Pulumi Cloud.

verdicts.text: An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
verdicts.evidence: The linked anchor says: "Executable-based plugin packages are usually distributed as pre-built per-language SDKs published to multiple package managers (one per consumer language), with the plugin executable published to an accessible location." The claim says the same thing. Its list of specific feeds (NuGet, Maven, Go proxy, private feeds) fits the source's "etc." and its note that pre-publishing SDKs is optional.
verdicts.framing_note: Source 'usually distributed as pre-built per-language SDKs ... with the plugin executable' vs claim 'pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs': same meaning, reworded. Only corroborated by another pulumi.com page, so confidence is medium.

verdicts.text: In both cases (source-based and executable-based), the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
verdicts.evidence: This is a summary of the page's own L17–28 description, so it can't serve as its own evidence. I tried to check it against pulumi/pulumi source (whether `pulumi package publish` requires semver), but the search hit a GitHub API rate limit (HTTP 403), and packaging-components.md, the sibling page I read, never says both package types ship as a single semver artifact.
verdicts.intuition_flag: L24 of the same page says source-based packages "can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version" — so "semantically-versioned" is true only for semver-tagged or Private Registry releases, not for every source-based package.

verdicts.text: A repository that contains multiple Pulumi packages either has to release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
verdicts.evidence: This is mostly Pulumi's own editorial reasoning. It follows from the page's premise that a source-based package's version is the repo's Git tag, but "fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages" is a judgment call. My gh searches of pulumi/pulumi PRs and issues found nothing on subdirectory or path-prefixed tag support that would confirm or refute it.
verdicts.source: repo:content/docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/repository-strategy.md L19-34; gh search prs/issues --repo pulumi/pulumi (no results)
verdicts.intuition_flag: The "either/or" framing may overstate things if Pulumi resolves path-prefixed tags (e.g. `subdir/v1.2.3`) for packages in subdirectories. Worth asking a pulumi/pulumi maintainer.

verdicts.text: A 1:1 repository-to-package mapping keeps git tags, release artifacts, and version history aligned.
verdicts.evidence: L34 is the rationale behind Pulumi's own recommendation ("A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package... The package is the unit of versioning and release"). The sentence argues why a 1:1 mapping is a good practice. It does not describe product behavior that can be tested.
verdicts.framing_note: Prescriptive best-practice rationale in Pulumi's own guidance, not a third-party-attributed or product-behavior assertion.

verdicts.text: Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are fine and expected, and the components ship together at the package's version.
verdicts.evidence: In the Pulumi Package Schema reference, `version` is a field on the package only ("Version is the version of the package. The version must be valid semver."). Resources, including components (`isComponent: true`), sit together in the package's `resources` map, and no resource has its own version field. So several components can live in one package and they share the package's version.
verdicts.framing_note: "Fine and expected" is the page's own recommendation, not a checkable fact. The checkable part is that components share the package's version, and the schema structure backs that up. I couldn't check pkg/codegen/schema/pulumi.json directly because GitHub rate-limited the search.

verdicts.text: The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
verdicts.evidence: The cited page loads (HTTP 200) and confirms the package exists ("I want to use the Pulumi Amazon EKS package (eks) in my project", published by Pulumi, repository pulumi/pulumi-eks). The fetched text is cut off, though, and doesn't list what the package contains, so it doesn't show that it bundles a cluster component plus supporting components for securing and running it.
verdicts.framing_note: The fetched text only covers package metadata (name, version, publisher, repository). The passage listing its components was not in the fetched content.
verdicts.intuition_flag: It's likely true: pulumi-eks ships Cluster, NodeGroup, ManagedNodeGroup and VpcCni components. The pulumi/pulumi-eks schema could confirm this.

verdicts.text: A single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
verdicts.evidence: The PulumiPlugin.yaml reference says the manifest "sits at the root of a source-based component package", and the source-based plugin guide says "Every component in the package is available under the generated SDK". Together these back the claim that one root manifest defines a package holding several components.
verdicts.framing_note: The reference page states the general rule (the manifest sits at the package root). The claim applies it to one example repo (eks-platform) where components sit under components/. The live repository-strategy page is the file under review, so it was not used as evidence.

verdicts.text: The example repository layout places `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repo root and components in a `components/` directory (EksCluster/, EksIam/).
verdicts.evidence: This describes the author's own example layout, which isn't something you can check against a source. Lines 58–65 show `eks-platform/` with `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the root and `components/` holding `EksCluster/` and `EksIam/`, so the claim restates the page correctly.

verdicts.text: When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way, regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.
verdicts.evidence: (re-verified after own-file-only) This is Pulumi's own advice on how to split packages across repos, not a product spec. The mechanical part, that components share their package's single version, is just what the page defines at L11 ("the components inside it inherit the package's version"). "Violates semver" is the author's opinion, and no product source can settle it.
verdicts.source: repo:content/docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/repository-strategy.md L69-81 (context only, not used as evidence)
verdicts.intuition_flag: "Violates semver" may be too strong. Semver versions a package's public API as a whole, so releasing a new package version with some components unchanged doesn't break the semver spec. It only makes the version less useful as a signal for each component. Consider softening to "undermines the signal semver provides."

verdicts.text: In a package containing ComponentA and ComponentB, an enhancement to ComponentA leads to release v1.1.0 and a breaking change to ComponentB leads to v2.0.0, decoupling the version from each component's evolution.
verdicts.evidence: L75-81 is a made-up example sequence ("Consider this sequence with two unrelated components...") showing how semver bumps work when components share a package. It doesn't describe any real Pulumi release. The version numbers follow standard semver: minor bump for an enhancement, major bump for a breaking change.

verdicts.text: Splitting unrelated components across separate, right-sized packages preserves the semver contract.
verdicts.evidence: This is the guide's own advice on how to lay out repositories, drawn from its argument in L73-80, not a checkable statement about how the product behaves. The factual premise it rests on, that each package is released as "a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package" (L30), is general semver reasoning rather than product source.

verdicts.evidence: The target file exists at content/docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages.md, in the same iac-guides-packages menu section, so the link resolves.
